blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how businesses keep track of all their customers' and suppliers' transactions? Control accounts are key to this process.

blocks.markdown: Control accounts serve as a summary of transactions that occur in the sales and purchases ledgers. They help businesses verify the accuracy of individual ledger accounts and detect errors.

blocks.title: Definition of Control Accounts
blocks.text: Control accounts are ledger accounts that summarize the total balances of individual accounts in the sales and purchases ledgers.

blocks.markdown: There are two main types of control accounts: the sales ledger control account and the purchases ledger control account. The sales ledger control account summarizes all transactions related to credit sales, while the purchases ledger control account summarizes all transactions related to credit purchases.

blocks.title: Preparing a Sales Ledger Control Account
blocks.prompt: Prepare a sales ledger control account using the following information: Total credit sales: ₦500,000, Returns inward: ₦20,000, Bad debts written off: ₦5,000, Cash received from debtors: ₦450,000.

steps.text: Start with the total credit sales as the opening balance on the debit side.
Subtract returns inward and bad debts written off from the debit side.
Subtract cash received from debtors from the debit side to find the closing balance.

blocks.answer: The closing balance of the sales ledger control account is ₦25,000.

blocks.markdown: A debit balance in the purchases ledger indicates that the business owes money to suppliers, while a credit balance in the sales ledger indicates that customers owe money to the business.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Always check that the totals of your control accounts match the totals of the individual accounts in the ledgers. This helps in identifying any discrepancies or errors.

points: Control accounts help in summarizing and verifying the accuracy of transactions in the sales and purchases ledgers.
A debit balance in the purchases ledger means the business owes suppliers, while a credit balance in the sales ledger means customers owe the business.
